newsitem.title: LIBERIA: U.S. airlifts West African peacekeepers to Liberia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlifts West African peacekeepers to Liberia.

text.p: U.S. planes began airlifting additional West African peacekeepers to Liberia on Tuesday, ahead of national elections in the shattered West African nation on May 30.
Witnesses said a first batch of 70 Ghanaians arrived from Ghana's capital Accra at the Robertsfield international airport 30 miles (50 km) east of Monrovia.
"The first trip today involved three aircraft, one carrying only troops and two containing just equipment," U.S. military spokesman Major Vic Warzinski told journalists.
The reinforcements will boost the Nigerian-led West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG to 12,000 men.
About 200 Marines are involved in the airlift, which will shuttle between Liberia and Ivory Coast, the base for the operation, and Ghana and Mali. They are using C-130 transport planes.

A total of 500 extra soldiers from Ghana will boost its contingent to 1,336 men. The planes will ferry in 600 soldiers from Mali and a 90-strong medical team from Ivory Coast. Burkina Faso is also due to send in 320 soldiers.
Under a peace deal brokered by its neighbours, Liberia will hold presidential and parliamentary elections on May 30 to end seven years of civil war.
ECOMOG commander General Victor Malu says he is satisfied with the level of disarmament of the faction fighters after that part of the countdown to peace ended earlier this month.
Founded by freed American slaves in 1847, Liberia has strong emotional ties with the United States.
A U.S. naval task force airlifted U.S. and other foreign nationals out of the capital Monrovia last April and May during a flare-up of the war in the capital.
